thread:
maya (Support): Hey @devon — I pulled up SUP-95431. Can you paste the exact curl or fetch call you used? logs only show a 415/422 and an HTML body.
devon (Customer): sure. From our browser SPA it fails, but here’s the server curl we used to repro:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"send me JSON","response_format":"json","strict":true}'

Server gives HTTP/1.1 415 and returns an HTML error page (starts with <!doctype) so our client parse crashes. This started after weekend deploy.
maya (Support): thanks. Do you set any Accept or custom headers in the browser? Are you calling from client or server?
devon (Customer): browser fetch from the SPA. We don't set Accept explicitly — using default fetch behavior. From Node (server) we sometimes see 502 + HTML too.
li (Eng-ML): tagging eng-runtime. HTML slip-through suggests upstream/edge returned an error page rather than a JSON error. Can you capture full response headers?
devon (Customer): minimal capture pasted below:

HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 1123

(body contains nginx error template)

Also noticed OPTIONS preflight returns 204 but Access-Control-Allow-Headers does NOT list Accept or Response-Format.
sam (Eng-Infra): if preflight doesn't allow Accept, the browser will strip non-simple headers. That can change the route through edge. @li maybe strict enforcement is running before CORS, causing HTML fallback.
li (Eng-ML): two hypotheses: 1) runtime expects Accept or explicit response-format header; if missing, strict enforcement rejects and we get HTML fallback, 2) CORS preflight path causes header stripping so the request follows a different codepath and the upstream edge returns HTML.

Repro steps (eng):
1) curl without Accept: curl -X POST ... -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{..."response_format":"json","strict":true}' -> 415 + html
2) curl with Accept: application/json -> 200 + structured JSON
3) browser fetch without explicit headers -> fails intermittently (depends on preflight)

maya (Support): customer reported a billing spike — frontend retried on parse error causing ~12x token charges.
devon (Customer): yes, our client retries every 2s for 6 attempts. Hugely expensive. Need mitigation ASAP.
sam (Eng-Infra): immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Set Accept: application/json (or application/specific+json) in browser fetch.
- Include response_format=structured_json in the body or Response-Format header if your client supports it.
- Temporarily disable strict=true to avoid hard parse enforcement while we investigate.
- Add client-side exponential backoff and dedupe to avoid a retry storm.

li (Eng-ML): we'll reproduce and audit edge ordering. @sam please check CORS preflight ACL to ensure Accept and response-format headers are allowed. Also verify whether strict-mode enforcement is executed at the edge before CORS handling — if so it should return a JSON error, not HTML.
sam (Eng-Infra): creating INF-4129 and escalating to oncall. I'll push a temporary CORS rule to include Accept and Response-Format for the affected route. ETA ~2 hours for the temporary rule; full runtime patch 1-2 days. Marking P1 due to billing impact.
maya (Support): told Devon how to apply the suggested headers and to pause retries. Please provide ETA so I can update the customer.
sam (Eng-Infra): confirmed: after adding Accept to Access-Control-Allow-Headers, browser call with explicit Accept now returns 200 and structured JSON. Holding runtime patch in the 2-day fix stream.
li (Eng-ML): additional note: customer previously used response_format="json" (a generic token). Runtime prefers explicit profile names like "structured_json"; mismatch can trigger schema negotiation mismatches. I'll add a regression test to ensure HTML never slips through when strict=true.
devon (Customer): thanks. What's the minimal header set you'd recommend for browser fetch to avoid surprises?
maya (Support): recommended minimal headers for browser clients:
- Accept: application/specific+json; profile="structured"
- Content-Type: application/json
- X-Request-ID: <uuid> (optional, helps tracing)
And include response_format=structured_json in the payload when using strict enforcement.
devon (Customer): applying now and pausing retries. Will report back if anything else.
maya (Support): keeping this thread updated. Support ticket SUP-95431. Tagging billing for review of possible credits.
billing-bot: SUP-95431 flagged for billing review; include request IDs if you want a charge reversal.

sam (Eng-Infra) (later): temporary allow-header rule deployed. Verified browser calls with Accept succeed. We'll follow up with runtime patch to ensure machine-readable errors in all paths.

(END)
